subject: astronomy
title: Earth, Moon & Sun: The Year
welcome_lead: 365 spins, one orbit — that's a year on Earth.
meta_desc: KS3 astronomy: Earth's orbit, the year, why leap years exist.
final_note: We need the extra day every 4 years to keep calendars tidy.

concepts.def: One orbit of Earth around the Sun.
A year with 366 days — adds Feb 29.
System that organises days into months and years.
Solar system has the Sun at the middle.

walkthroughs.body_html: Earth completes one orbit around the Sun in about 365.25 days. Each orbit is what we call a year.
That extra 0.25 day means after 4 years we're a day behind. So every 4 years we add Feb 29 — a leap year.
Earth's orbit is nearly a circle but slightly oval. The distance changes a little through the year — but that's not what makes seasons.
